summary: James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He studied at Cambridge, Oxford under Benson, Gombrich, and Sanderson, and earned his PhD at Harvard under McCrea, Monius, and Patil. He held posts at USC and Cornell University.

James Miller is a scholar of Sinology and religious studies. He earned an MA from the University of Cambridge by 1997 and a PhD from Boston University by 2000. By 2014, he was Professor of Chinese Studies and Religious Studies at Queen's University Belfast.
James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as librarian at the Indian Institute, University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Murdoch (1856–1921) was a scholar of Japanology and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1875–1879) and under Theodor Benfey (~1878–1879). He held posts at the University of Tokyo, Kanazawa University, and Kagoshima University.

James Prinsep (1799–1840) was an Indology and history/archaeology scholar. He worked at the Benares and Kolkata Mints, led The Asiatic Society (1832–1838), and founded the Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal and Corpus Inscriptionum Indicarum.

James Robert Ballantyne (1813–1864) worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. Educated at the University of Edinburgh and taught by James Michael and Francis Johnson, he served as master at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and librarian at the India Office.

James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and Stanford (PhD). He taught at Williams College and the University of Michigan before becoming a professor at Harvard and director of the Harvard-Yenching Institute.

James Smith Reid (1846–1926) was an archaeology and history scholar who studied at the University of Cambridge (~1865–1869). He held academic posts at Christ's College, Pembroke College, and Gonville and Caius College, Cambridge.

James Sutherland Cotton (1847–1918) was a historian and Indologist. Educated at Winchester College and Trinity College, Oxford (1867–1870), he held posts at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1871–1874) and Queens' College, Cambridge (1871–1874).

James Tod (1782–1835) was an Indologist and historian. He studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich, and under Gyanchandra (~1812–1822). He served in the East India Company (~1798–1822) and as Librarian of the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).

James W. Benson is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He held faculty posts at Harvard University (attested 1999) and the University of Oxford, including Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 1999, 2001).

James W. Heisig is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. He earned degrees from Divine Word College, Loyola University Chicago, Notre Dame, and Cambridge. He was a longtime Permanent Research Fellow at Nanzan University and its Institute for Religion and Culture.
James Ward (1843–1925) was a philosopher who studied at Fitzwilliam College and Trinity College, Cambridge. He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1925.
James Whitehill is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He founded the Columbia Zen Center and served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

James Wilson Bright (1852–1926) was a linguist who studied at Lafayette College and Johns Hopkins University (PhD). He taught briefly at Cornell University and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins University (1905–1925).

Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso (1846–1912) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. He studied under prominent masters including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye, and taught numerous students.

Jamgon Kongtrul Lodro Chokyi Senge (1954–1992) was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies figure. He studied under the 16th Karmapa, Kalu Rinpoche, Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Nyoshul Khenpo Rinpoche, and taught Richard Barron and Jampa Mackenzie Stewart.

Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye (1813–1899) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master. He studied under numerous teachers, notably Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, and Tai Situ Pema Nyinje Wangpo, and also taught figures such as Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa.

Jamie Hubbard is a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar. He studied at Komazawa University and earned a PhD from the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Minoru Kiyota. He held named professorships at Smith College, where he is now professor emeritus.
Jampa Lhundup is a scholar in Tibetology and linguistics. He is attested as faculty and Assistant Professor of Art History at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).
